translations.literal: Zhao Huai
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Huai

sentences.zh: 初，親戚有勸其移治者，元桂曰：“子亦為浮議所搖耶？

translations.literal: At first, relatives had urged him to relocate his administration. Yuangui said, "Are you also swayed by idle talk?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, kinsmen had urged him to move his seat of government elsewhere. Yuangui said, "Are you swayed by loose talk as well?

sentences.zh: 時事如此，與其死於饑饉，死於疾病，死於盜賊，孰若死於守土之為光明俊偉哉？”

translations.literal: The times are as they are. Rather than die of famine, die of illness, or die at the hands of bandits, how is dying in defense of one's charge not the more bright and noble course?"
translations.idiomatic: These are the times we live in. Better to die holding this post than to die of famine, sickness, or bandits — what death could be brighter or more worthy?"

sentences.zh: 家人或請登舟，不許，且戒之曰：“守臣家屬豈可先動，以搖民心。”

translations.literal: When his family asked to board boats, he would not allow it and admonished them, saying, "How can the household of a defending official move first and shake the people's hearts?"
translations.idiomatic: When his family asked to board boats and flee, he refused and warned them, "How can a defending official's household leave first and unsettle the people?"

sentences.zh: 敏子以聞，贈寶章閣待制，賜緡錢十萬，與一子京官、一子選人恩澤，立廟北門，諡曰正節。

translations.literal: Minzi reported it to the throne. [Yuangui] was posthumously made Baozhangge Attendant-in-Waiting, granted one hundred thousand strings of cash, one son given a capital-office appointment and one son selector's preferment, a temple was established at the north gate, and his posthumous title was Zhengjie (Upright Integrity).
translations.idiomatic: Minzi reported his death to court. Yuangui was posthumously appointed Baozhangge Attendant-in-Waiting, granted one hundred thousand strings of cash, one son received a capital-office appointment and another selector's preferment, a shrine was raised at the north gate, and he was given the posthumous title Upright Integrity.

sentences.zh: 張順，民兵部將也。

translations.literal: Zhang Shun was a deputy commander in the Militia Department.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shun served as a deputy commander in the militia bureau.

sentences.zh: 襄陽受圍五年，宋闖知其西北一水曰清泥河，源於均、房，即其地造輕舟百艘，以三舟聯為一舫，中一舟裝載，左右舟則虛其底而掩覆之。

translations.literal: Xiangyang had been besieged for five years. The Song learned of a stream to its northwest called the Qingni River, which rose in Jun and Fang. At that place they built one hundred light boats, linking three boats into one craft: the middle boat carried cargo, while the boats to left and right had hollowed bottoms and were covered over.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiangyang had been under siege for five years, the Song discovered a waterway to the northwest called the Qingni River, rising in Jun and Fang. There they built a hundred light vessels, joining three into one flotilla — the center boat laden, the flanking boats hollowed beneath and decked over.

sentences.zh: 出重賞募死士，得三千。

translations.literal: They offered heavy rewards to recruit men willing to die and obtained three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rewards were posted to recruit men ready to die; three thousand answered.

sentences.zh: 求將，得順與張貴，俗呼順曰“矮張”，貴曰“竹園張”，俱智勇，素為諸將所服，俾為都統。

translations.literal: Seeking commanders, they obtained Shun and Zhang Gui. The common people called Shun "Short Zhang" and Gui "Bamboo Garden Zhang." Both were wise and brave and long respected by the generals, and they were made overall commanders.
translations.idiomatic: When leaders were sought, Shun and Zhang Gui were chosen. Folk called Shun "Short Zhang" and Gui "Bamboo Garden Zhang." Both were clever and daring, long trusted by the other commanders, and were appointed joint commanders-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 出令曰：“此行有死而已，汝輩或非本心，宜亟去，毋敗吾事。”

translations.literal: They issued an order, saying, "On this mission there is only death. If any of you are not of one heart, you should leave at once and not ruin our undertaking."
translations.idiomatic: They proclaimed, "This voyage ends only in death. If any among you lack true resolve, leave now — do not ruin what we mean to do."

sentences.zh: 人人感奮。

translations.literal: Every man was stirred and inspired.
translations.idiomatic: Every man was stirred to fervor.

sentences.zh: 漢水方生，發舟百艘，稍進團山下。

translations.literal: When the Han River was rising, they launched the hundred boats and advanced a little to below Tuan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: As the Han swelled, the hundred boats set out and edged forward to the foot of Tuan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 越二日，進高頭港口，結方陳，各船置火槍、火炮、熾炭、巨斧、勁弩。

translations.literal: After two days they advanced to Gaotou Harbor, formed a square formation, and on each boat placed fire-lances, cannon, blazing coals, great axes, and powerful crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later they reached Gaotou Harbor, drew up in square formation, and armed each vessel with fire-lances, cannon, hot coals, heavy axes, and strong crossbows.

sentences.zh: 夜漏下三刻，起矴出江，以紅燈為識。

translations.literal: At the third quarter after midnight they raised anchor and went out on the river, using red lamps as signals.
translations.idiomatic: In the third quarter of the night watch they weighed anchor and entered the river, red lanterns serving as their signals.

sentences.zh: 貴先登，順殿之，乘風破浪，徑犯重圍。

translations.literal: Gui led the advance and Shun brought up the rear. Riding wind and cleaving waves, they charged straight through the heavy encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: Gui took the lead and Shun closed the rear. They rode wind and broke waves, driving straight into the thick of the blockade.

sentences.zh: 至磨洪灘以上，北軍舟師布滿江麵，無隙可入。

translations.literal: Above Mohong Shoals the Northern Army's fleet filled the river surface, with no gap by which to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Above Mohong Shoals the northern fleet covered the river, leaving no opening.

sentences.zh: 眾乘銳凡斷鐵縆攢杙數百，轉戰百二十里，黎明抵襄城下。

translations.literal: The men, riding their sharp momentum, cut through several hundred iron cables and piled stakes, fought their way for one hundred twenty li, and at dawn reached below Xiang city.
translations.idiomatic: Riding their momentum, they severed hundreds of iron cables and clustered stakes, fought a hundred and twenty li, and at dawn reached the walls of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 城中久絕援，聞救至，踴躍氣百倍。

translations.literal: The city had long been cut off from relief. Hearing that rescue had come, the men leaped for joy and their spirit increased a hundredfold.
translations.idiomatic: The city had long gone without relief. When word of rescue came, men leapt for joy and their spirit swelled a hundredfold.

sentences.zh: 及收軍，獨失順。

translations.literal: When the force withdrew, Shun alone was missing.
translations.idiomatic: When the force withdrew, Shun alone was lost.

sentences.zh: 越數日，有浮屍溯流而上，被介胄，執弓矢，直抵浮梁，視之順也，身中四槍六箭，怒氣勃勃如生。

translations.literal: Several days later a floating corpse came upstream. It wore armor, held bow and arrows, and came straight to the pontoon bridge. When they looked, it was Shun. His body had taken four spears and six arrows, yet his wrathful spirit surged as if he were alive.
translations.idiomatic: Days later a body floated upstream in armor, bow in hand, drifting straight to the pontoon bridge. It was Shun — four spear wounds, six arrow wounds — yet his wrathful bearing still blazed as though he lived.

sentences.zh: 諸軍驚以為神，結塚斂葬，立廟祀之。

translations.literal: The armies were astonished and took him for a spirit. They built a mound, gathered him for burial, and established a temple to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: The troops marveled, deeming him divine. They raised a mound, buried him with honor, and founded a shrine in his name.

sentences.zh: 張貴既抵襄，襄帥呂文煥力留共守。

translations.literal: After Zhang Gui reached Xiang, the Xiang commander Lü Wenhuan pressed him hard to stay and defend together.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhang Gui reached Xiangyang, its commander Lü Wenhuan pressed him to remain and defend the city together.

sentences.zh: 貴恃其驍勇，欲還郢，乃募二士能伏水中數日不食，使持蠟書赴郢求援。

translations.literal: Gui relied on his fierce courage and wished to return to Ying. He recruited two men able to lie submerged in water for days without eating and sent them with wax-sealed letters to Ying to seek aid.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his daring, Gui wished to return to Ying. He recruited two men who could stay underwater for days without food and sent them with wax-sealed dispatches to Ying to beg for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 北兵增守益密，水路連鎖數十里，列撒星樁，雖魚蝦不得度。

translations.literal: The Northern Army increased its defenses ever tighter. The water route was chained for several tens of li, with scattered-star stakes set in rows, so that not even fish or shrimp could pass.
translations.idiomatic: The northern forces tightened their blockade. The waterway was chained for tens of li, studded with stake barriers so dense that not even fish could pass.

sentences.zh: 二人遇樁即鋸斷之，竟達郢，還報，許發兵五千駐龍尾洲以助夾擊。

translations.literal: Whenever the two men met a stake they sawed it through. They finally reached Ying, returned with word, and were promised five thousand troops stationed at Longwei Shoal to assist in a pincer attack.
translations.idiomatic: The pair sawed through every stake they met, reached Ying at last, and returned with word that five thousand troops would be posted at Longwei Shoal for a joint strike.

sentences.zh: 刻日既定，乃別文煥東下，點視所部軍，洎登舟，帳前一人亡去，乃有過被撻者。

translations.literal: Once the day was fixed, he took leave of Wenhuan and went east downstream, mustering his troops. Just as he boarded his boat, one man before his tent fled — a man who had been flogged for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: With the day set, he bade Wenhuan farewell and sailed east to muster his men. As he boarded, a man from before his tent vanished — one recently flogged for a fault.

sentences.zh: 貴驚曰：“吾事泄矣，亟行，彼或未及知。”

translations.literal: Gui said in alarm, "Our plan has leaked. Move at once — they may not yet know."
translations.idiomatic: Gui cried in alarm, "Our plan is out. Sail now — they may not yet know."

sentences.zh: 復不能銜枚隱跡，乃舉炮鼓噪發舟，乘夜順流斷縆破圍冒進，眾皆辟易。

translations.literal: Yet he could no longer keep silence and hide his tracks. He ordered cannon fired and drums beaten in uproar as the boats set out. Riding the night current downstream, they cut cables, broke the encirclement, and charged forward. All gave way before them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet silence was impossible. Cannon thundered and drums roared as the fleet launched. Under cover of night they ran downstream, cutting cables and smashing through the blockade; all who met them gave way.

sentences.zh: 既出險地，夜半天黑，至小新城，大兵邀擊，以死拒戰。

translations.literal: After they left the dangerous ground, it was midnight and pitch dark. They reached Little New City, where the great army intercepted them. They fought to the death in resistance.
translations.idiomatic: Clear of the narrows at midnight in utter dark, they reached Little New City, where the main force intercepted them. They fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 沿岸束荻列炬，火光燭天如白晝。

translations.literal: Along the banks reeds were bound and torches arrayed; firelight lit the sky bright as day.
translations.idiomatic: Reed bundles lined the banks, torches blazing until the sky shone white as noon.

sentences.zh: 至勾林灘，漸近龍尾洲，遙望軍船旗幟紛披，貴軍喜躍，舉流星火示之。

translations.literal: At Goulin Shoal, as they drew near Longwei Shoal, they saw in the distance military boats with banners fluttering. Gui's force leaped for joy and raised signal fire to show themselves.
translations.idiomatic: At Goulin Shoal, nearing Longwei Shoal, they sighted distant warships with banners flying. Gui's men leapt for joy and raised signal fires.

sentences.zh: 軍船見火即前迎，及勢近欲合，則來舟皆北兵也。

translations.literal: The military boats, seeing the fire, came forward to meet them. But as they drew near and were about to join, the approaching vessels were all Northern Army ships.
translations.idiomatic: The fleet saw the signal and came to meet them — but as they closed to join, every approaching vessel was northern.

sentences.zh: 蓋郢兵前二日以風水驚疑，退屯三十里，而大兵得逃卒之報，據龍尾洲以逸待勞。

translations.literal: For the Ying troops, alarmed two days earlier by wind and water, had withdrawn and encamped thirty li away, while the great army, learning from the deserter's report, held Longwei Shoal and waited at ease for their weary foe.
translations.idiomatic: Two days earlier Ying's troops, unnerved by wind and current, had fallen back thirty li, while the main force, warned by the deserter, held Longwei Shoal and waited fresh for their weary enemy.

sentences.zh: 貴戰已困，出於不意，殺傷殆盡，身被數十槍，力不支見執，卒不屈，死之。

translations.literal: Gui's force was already exhausted from battle. Caught unawares, they were nearly all killed or wounded. His body took several tens of spear wounds. Unable to hold out, he was seized, yet in the end he did not submit and died.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's men were already spent. Caught off guard, they were nearly annihilated. He took dozens of wounds, collapsed, and was taken — yet would not yield and died.

sentences.zh: 乃命降卒四人舁屍至襄，令於城下曰：“識矮張乎？

translations.literal: They then ordered four surrendered soldiers to carry the corpse to Xiang and call out below the wall, "Do you know Short Zhang?
translations.idiomatic: Four surrendered soldiers were ordered to carry his body to Xiangyang and call beneath the wall, "Do you know Short Zhang?

sentences.zh: 此是也。”

translations.literal: This is he."
translations.idiomatic: Here he is."

sentences.zh: 守陴者皆哭，城中喪氣。

translations.literal: The men on the battlements all wept, and the city's spirit collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Men on the walls wept, and the city's spirit broke.

sentences.zh: 文煥斬四卒，以貴祔葬順塚，立雙廟祀之。

translations.literal: Wenhuan executed the four soldiers, buried Gui beside Shun's mound in joint burial, and established twin temples to worship them.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhuan executed the four soldiers, buried Gui beside Shun's tomb, and raised twin shrines to both.

sentences.zh: 範天順，荊湖都統也。

translations.literal: Fan Tianshun was commander-in-chief of Jinghu.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tianshun was the Jinghu regional commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 襄陽受圍，天順日夕守戰尤力。

translations.literal: When Xiangyang was besieged, Tianshun defended and fought day and night with especial vigor.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege of Xiangyang, Tianshun fought at the walls day and night with exceptional zeal.

sentences.zh: 及呂文煥出降，天順仰天歎曰：“生為宋臣，死當為宋鬼。”

translations.literal: When Lü Wenhuan came out to surrender, Tianshun looked up to heaven and sighed, "Alive I was a Song subject; dead I shall be a Song ghost."
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Wenhuan surrendered, Tianshun looked skyward and sighed, "Alive I served the Song; dead I shall be a Song ghost."

sentences.zh: 即所守處縊死。

translations.literal: He then hanged himself at the post he had defended.
translations.idiomatic: He hanged himself on the spot he had held.

sentences.zh: 贈定江軍承宣使，製曰：“賀蘭擁兵，坐視睢陽之失；

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Military Commissioner of the Dingjiang Army. The edict said, "Helan held troops yet sat by and watched the fall of Suiyang;
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Military Commissioner of the Dingjiang Army. The edict read, "Helan held his army yet watched Suiyang fall;

sentences.zh: 李陵失節，重為隴士之羞。

translations.literal: Li Ling lost his integrity and became again a shame to the gentlemen of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ling broke faith and brought fresh shame on the men of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 今有人焉，得其死所，可無褒恤，以示寵綏？

translations.literal: Now there is one who has found his place of death — shall we not grant reward and consolation to show favor and reassurance?
translations.idiomatic: Now here is one who found his proper death — shall we not honor and comfort him to show imperial favor?

sentences.zh: 範天順功烈雖卑，忠義莫奪，自均、房泛舟之役克濟於艱，而襄、樊坐甲之師益堅所守。

translations.literal: Fan Tianshun's achievements were humble, yet his loyalty and righteousness could not be taken away. From the boat expedition launched at Jun and Fang he overcame hardship, and the armies sitting in armor at Xiang and Fan grew firmer in what they held.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tianshun's deeds were modest, yet his loyalty was unshakable. From the boat mission out of Jun and Fang he prevailed through hardship, and the garrisons at Xiangyang and Fancheng held all the firmer.

sentences.zh: 俄州刺史為降將軍，爾乃不屈自經，可謂見危致命。”

translations.literal: Soon the Ezhou prefect became a surrendered general, yet he would not submit and hanged himself — this may be called meeting peril and giving one's life."
translations.idiomatic: When the Ezhou prefect became a surrendered general, he refused to yield and hanged himself — truly meeting danger and giving his life."

sentences.zh: 封其妻宜人，官其二子，仍賜白金五百兩，田五百畝。

translations.literal: His wife was enfeoffed as Yiren, his two sons were given offices, and there were further granted five hundred taels of white silver and five hundred mu of fields.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was enfeoffed as Lady Yiren, both sons received offices, and five hundred taels of silver and five hundred mu of land were granted besides.

sentences.zh: 牛富，霍丘人。

translations.literal: Niu Fu was a man of Huoqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Fu came from Huoqiu.

sentences.zh: 制置司遊擊砦兵籍。

translations.literal: He was on the roster of the Pacification Commission's mobile camp troops.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the roster of the Pacification Commission's raiding camp.

sentences.zh: 勇而知義。

translations.literal: He was brave and understood righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Brave and mindful of duty.

sentences.zh: 為侍衛馬軍司統制。

translations.literal: He became Controller of the Palace Guard Horse Army.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to controller of the Palace Guard Horse Army.

sentences.zh: 戍襄陽五年，移守樊城，累戰不為衄，且數射書襄陽城中遺呂文煥，相與固守為唇齒。

translations.literal: He garrisoned Xiangyang for five years, then moved to defend Fancheng. In repeated battles he was not driven back, and several times shot letters into Xiang city to Lü Wenhuan, the two holding firm together like lips and teeth.
translations.idiomatic: He garrisoned Xiangyang five years, then shifted to Fancheng. Battle after battle he held his ground, and repeatedly shot messages into Xiangyang to Lü Wenhuan so the two cities stood firm together like lips and teeth.

sentences.zh: 兩城凡六年不拔，富力居多。

translations.literal: The two cities for six years in all could not be taken, and Fu's strength counted for much of this.
translations.idiomatic: For six years neither city fell — Fu's strength bore much of the credit.

sentences.zh: 城破，富率死士百人巷戰，死傷不可計，渴飲血水。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Fu led a hundred men willing to die in street fighting. The dead and wounded were countless. Parched with thirst, they drank bloody water.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Fu led a hundred die-hards into the alleys. Casualties were beyond counting; parched, they drank bloody water.

sentences.zh: 轉戰前，遇民居燒絕街道，身被重傷，以頭觸柱赴火死。

translations.literal: Fighting forward, they came to dwellings burned out along the street. His body took grave wounds. He dashed his head against a pillar and threw himself into the fire to die.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting forward through streets burned bare, he took grave wounds, dashed his head against a pillar, and threw himself into the flames.

sentences.zh: 贈靜江軍節度使，諡忠烈，賜廟建康。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Military Governor of the Jingjiang Army, given the posthumous title Zhonglie (Loyal and Fierce), and granted a temple at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Military Governor of the Jingjiang Army, titled Loyal and Fierce, and granted a shrine at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 裨將王福見富死，歎曰：“將軍死國事，吾豈宜獨生！”

translations.literal: The deputy commander Wang Fu, seeing Fu die, sighed and said, "The general has died for the state — how should I alone live!"
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander Wang Fu, seeing Fu die, sighed, "Our general died for the realm — how can I live on alone?"

sentences.zh: 亦赴火死。

translations.literal: He too threw himself into the fire and died.
translations.idiomatic: He too cast himself into the fire and died.

sentences.zh: 邊居誼，隨人也。

translations.literal: Bian Juyi was a man of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Juyi came from Sui prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初事李庭芝，積戰功至都統製。

translations.literal: He first served Li Tingzhi and, accumulating battle merit, rose to Overall Controller.
translations.idiomatic: He first served under Li Tingzhi and, through accumulated battle honors, rose to overall controller.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳十年，以京湖製置帳前都統守新城。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianchun he served as Front Headquarters Overall Commander under the Jinghu Pacification Commission, defending New City.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Xianchun (1274) he was appointed front headquarters overall commander under the Jing-Hu Pacification Commission to defend New City.

sentences.zh: 居誼善禦下，得士心，凡戰守之具，治之皆有法。

translations.literal: Juyi was skilled in commanding subordinates and won the soldiers' hearts. Whatever was needed for attack or defense, he managed each with proper method.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi governed his men well and won their hearts. Every implement of war and defense he ordered by sound method.

sentences.zh: 大兵至沙陽，守將王大用不降，麾兵攻城，破之，執大用。

translations.literal: When the great army reached Shayang, the defending general Wang Dayong would not surrender. They waved the troops forward to attack the city, broke it, and seized Dayong.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force reached Shayang, defender Wang Dayong refused to yield. They stormed the city, took it, and seized Dayong.

sentences.zh: 呂文煥至新城，意其小壘可不攻而破，居誼率舟師拒之，文煥列沙陽所斬首招降，不從。

translations.literal: Lü Wenhuan came to New City, thinking its small fort could be taken without a fight. Juyi led the river force to resist him. Wenhuan displayed the heads cut off at Shayang to summon surrender, but Juyi would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wenhuan reached New City expecting the small fort to fall without a fight. Juyi led the river fleet against him. Wenhuan paraded heads taken at Shayang to demand surrender; Juyi refused.

sentences.zh: 明日，縛大用至壁下，使呼曰：“邊都統急降，不然禍即至矣。”

translations.literal: The next day they bound Dayong below the wall and made him call out, "Commander Bian, surrender at once, or disaster will come immediately."
translations.idiomatic: Next day they bound Dayong beneath the wall and made him shout, "Commander Bian, surrender now or ruin is upon you."

sentences.zh: 居誼不答。

translations.literal: Juyi did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi made no reply.

sentences.zh: 又射榜檄入壁中，居誼曰：“吾欲與呂參政語耳。”

translations.literal: They again shot proclamations into the wall. Juyi said, "I wish only to speak with Vice-Commissioner Lü."
translations.idiomatic: They shot proclamations over the wall. Juyi said, "I only wish to speak with Vice-Commissioner Lü."

sentences.zh: 文煥聞之，以為居誼降己也，馳馬至，伏弩亂發，中文煥者三，並中其馬，馬仆，幾鉤得之，眾挾文煥以他馬奔走。

translations.literal: Wenhuan heard this and thought Juyi was surrendering to him. He galloped up, but hidden crossbows fired in disorder. Wenhuan was hit three times, and his horse was hit as well. The horse fell. They nearly hooked and seized him, but the crowd seized Wenhuan onto another horse and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhuan heard this and thought Juyi meant to yield. He galloped up; hidden crossbows loosed in a volley. Wenhuan took three bolts, his horse several more. The horse fell; grappling hooks nearly took him, but his men dragged him onto another mount and fled.

sentences.zh: 越二日，總製黃順挾一人開東門走出降。

translations.literal: After two days the overall controller Huang Shun took a man with him, opened the east gate, and went out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later overall controller Huang Shun opened the east gate with a companion and went out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 明日，使順來招之，居誼曰：“若欲得新城邪？

translations.literal: The next day they sent Shun to summon him. Juyi said, "Do you wish to take New City?
translations.idiomatic: Next day they sent Shun to parley. Juyi said, "You want New City?

sentences.zh: 吾誓以死守此，何可得也。”

translations.literal: I have sworn to defend this place to the death — how can you obtain it?"
translations.idiomatic: I have sworn to hold it to the death — you shall not have it."

sentences.zh: 順又呼其部曲，部曲欲縋城出，居誼悉驅以入，當門斬之。

translations.literal: Shun again called out to his subordinate officers. The officers wished to lower themselves from the wall and flee. Juyi drove them all back inside and beheaded them before the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Shun called to his officers. Some tried to lower themselves over the wall to flee. Juyi drove them back in and beheaded them at the gate.

sentences.zh: 文煥乃麾兵攻城，以火具卻之，旋蟻附而上。

translations.literal: Wenhuan then waved the troops to attack the city. They were driven back with fire weapons, but soon they swarmed up like ants.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhuan ordered the assault. Fire weapons beat them back briefly, then they swarmed the walls like ants.

sentences.zh: 居誼乃取其家金盡散將士，往來督戰。

translations.literal: Juyi then took his family's gold, distributed it all to the soldiers, and went back and forth supervising the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi took his family's gold, gave it all to the troops, and ranged the walls urging them on.

sentences.zh: 會暮，破侵漢樓，樓火延毀民居，居誼度力不支，走還第，拔劍自殺，不殊，赴火死。

translations.literal: At dusk the Qinhan Tower was breached. Fire from the tower spread and destroyed dwellings. Juyi judged that strength could not hold. He ran back to his residence, drew his sword to kill himself but did not die outright, and threw himself into the fire to die.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the Qinhan Tower fell; flames spread through the town. Seeing resistance spent, Juyi ran home, tried to fall on his sword but did not die cleanly, and threw himself into the fire.

sentences.zh: 丞相伯顏壯其勇，購得其屍燼中，觀之。

translations.literal: The Chancellor Bayan admired his courage, purchased [the right to recover] his body from the ashes, and viewed it.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Bayan admired his courage, paid to recover his body from the ashes, and looked upon it.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈利州觀察使，立廟死所。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously made Regional Inspector of Lizhou, and a temple was established at the place of his death.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached court, he was posthumously made Regional Inspector of Lizhou and a shrine was raised where he died.

sentences.zh: 陳炤，字光伯，常州人。

translations.literal: Chen Zhao, style name Guangbo, was a man of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhao, styled Guangbo, came from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 少工詞賦，登第，為丹徒縣尉，曆兩淮製置司參議官、大軍倉曹壽春府教授，復入帥幕，改知朐山縣，仍兼主管機宜文字。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled at rhapsodies and fu. He passed the examinations, became magistrate of Dantu County, served successively as staff adviser of the Huai-East Pacification Commission, granary clerk and professor at the Shouchun prefectural school, reentered the commander's staff, was changed to magistrate of Qushan County, and still concurrently supervised confidential documents.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he excelled at regulated verse and fu. After passing the examinations he was magistrate of Dantu, then staff adviser on the Two Huai Pacification Commission, granary clerk and professor at Shouchun, returned to a commander's staff, became magistrate of Qushan, and still oversaw confidential papers.

sentences.zh: 尋丁母憂歸。

translations.literal: Soon he returned home on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned home to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 北兵至常，常守趙與鑒走匿，郡人錢訔以城降。

translations.literal: When the Northern Army reached Chang, the Chang prefect Zhao Yujian fled and hid. A man of the prefecture, Qian Yin, surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: When northern troops reached Changzhou, prefect Zhao Yujian fled into hiding and local man Qian Yin surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 淮民王通居常州，陰以書約劉師勇，許為內應。

translations.literal: Wang Tong, a Huai River native living in Changzhou, secretly sent a letter arranging with Liu Shiyong and promised to act as an inside collaborator.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tong, a Huai native living in Changzhou, secretly wrote Liu Shiyong pledging to serve as an inside contact.

sentences.zh: 朝議乃以姚希得子訔知常州。

translations.literal: Court deliberation then made Yao Xide's son Yin prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Court then appointed Yao Xide's son Yin prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 師通肋常州，走錢訔，執安撫戴之泰等，遂迎訔以入。

translations.literal: Shiyong and Tong pressured Changzhou, drove off Qian Yin, seized the pacification commissioner Dai Zhitan and others, and then welcomed Yin to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyong and Tong seized Changzhou, drove off Qian Yin, arrested pacification commissioner Dai Zhitan and others, and welcomed Yin into the city.

sentences.zh: 訔以照久任邊知兵，辟為通判。

translations.literal: Yin, because Zhao had long served on the frontier and understood warfare, summoned him as vice-prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, knowing Zhao's long frontier service and military knowledge, appointed him vice-prefect.

sentences.zh: 或謂照曰：“今辟難有辭矣。”

translations.literal: Someone said to Zhao, "Now you have a good excuse to avoid hardship."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Zhao, "Now you have a ready excuse to avoid danger."

sentences.zh: 照曰：“鄉邦淪沒，何可坐視，與其偷生而苟全，不若死之愈也。”

translations.literal: Zhao said, "Our native district has fallen — how can we sit and watch? Rather than steal life and preserve oneself in compromise, it is better to die."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao replied, "Our homeland is lost — how can we stand by? Better to die than live on in shame and safety."

sentences.zh: 遂墨衰而出。

translations.literal: He then put on mourning dress in ink-black and went out.
translations.idiomatic: He donned unhemmed mourning dress and went out to fight.

sentences.zh: 凡可以備禦者，無不為之。

translations.literal: Whatever could serve for defense, there was nothing he did not do.
translations.idiomatic: He left nothing undone that might serve defense.

sentences.zh: 訔入常甫十餘日，大軍攻常，照等率義兵戰禦，自夏徂冬不能下。

translations.literal: Yin had entered Chang only a little more than ten days when the great army attacked Chang. Zhao and others led volunteer troops to fight in defense. From summer to winter they could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Yin had held Changzhou barely ten days when the main force attacked. Zhao and others led militia in defense; from summer through winter the city would not fall.

sentences.zh: 以功加帶行提轄文思院。

translations.literal: For merit he was additionally given acting superintendent of the Wensi Court with belt insignia.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made acting superintendent of the Wensi Court with belt insignia.

sentences.zh: 常將張彥攻呂城，兵敗而降，因盡言常城中虛實，遂急攻之。

translations.literal: The Chang general Zhang Yan attacked Lücheng, was defeated and surrendered, and therefore told all the truth and falsehood within Chang city, whereupon they pressed the attack urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhou general Zhang Yan attacked Lücheng, was beaten and surrendered, and revealed the city's full situation — after which the assault intensified.

sentences.zh: 照等晝夜城守，招之不下。

translations.literal: Zhao and others defended the city day and night. Summons to surrender could not bring them down.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao and his men held the walls day and night and would not yield to summons.

sentences.zh: 丞相伯顏自將圍其城，照與訔持以忠義，協力固守。

translations.literal: The Chancellor Bayan personally led the siege of the city. Zhao and Yin upheld loyalty and righteousness and joined forces to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Bayan personally besieged the city. Zhao and Yin stood on loyalty and righteousness and held together.

sentences.zh: 再加訔太府寺丞，照幹辦諸軍糧料院，常將士皆轉五官。

translations.literal: Yin was further promoted to Vice Director of the Grand Storehouse Directorate, Zhao made staff officer of the Bureau for Provisions of All Armies, and the Chang officers and soldiers were all transferred up five ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was promoted to vice director of the Grand Storehouse, Zhao to staff officer of the army provisions bureau, and every Changzhou officer and soldier advanced five ranks.

sentences.zh: 城益急，常兵阻壕水為陳，矢盡亦不降。

translations.literal: As the siege grew more urgent, the Chang troops blocked the moat water to form a battle line. When arrows were exhausted they still would not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: As the siege tightened, defenders dammed the moat to form a battle line. When arrows ran out, they still would not yield.

sentences.zh: 城破，訔死之，照猶斂兵巷戰，家人請曰：“城東北門圍未合，可走常熟入臨安也。”

translations.literal: When the city fell, Yin died. Zhao still gathered troops for street fighting. His family pleaded, "The encirclement at the northeast gate is not yet closed — you can flee through Changshu to Lin'an."
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Yin died. Zhao still rallied men for street fighting. His family urged, "The northeast gate is not yet sealed — flee through Changshu to Lin'an."

sentences.zh: 照曰：“去此一步，非死所矣。”

translations.literal: Zhao said, "One step from here is no longer the place to die."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, "One step from here is no longer where a man should die."

sentences.zh: 日中兵至，死焉。

translations.literal: At midday the enemy arrived, and he died there.
translations.idiomatic: At midday the enemy came, and there he died.

sentences.zh: 事上，追贈訔龍圖閣待制，希得贈太師，照直寶章閣，並官其子。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported upward, Yin was posthumously made Longtu Attendant-in-Waiting, Xide posthumously made Grand Preceptor, Zhao made direct Baozhangge Attendant-in-Waiting, and their sons were all given offices.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached court, Yin was posthumously made Longtu Attendant-in-Waiting, Xide posthumously Grand Preceptor, Zhao direct Baozhangge attendant, and their sons received offices.

sentences.zh: 王安節，節度使堅之子也。

translations.literal: Wang Anjie was the son of Military Commissioner Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anjie was the son of Military Commissioner Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 少從其父守合州有功，安節等兄弟五人皆受官。

translations.literal: In youth he followed his father in defending Hezhou with merit. Anjie and his four brothers all received offices.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he followed his father in the successful defense of Hezhou. Anjie and his four brothers all received appointments.

sentences.zh: 堅為賈似道所忌，出知和州，鬱鬱而死。

translations.literal: Jian was envied by Jia Sidao, was sent out as prefect of Hezhou, and died in dejection.
translations.idiomatic: Jian earned Jia Sidao's enmity, was posted out as prefect of Hezhou, and died in grief.

sentences.zh: 安節至鹹淳末為東南第七副將。

translations.literal: At the end of Xianchun, Anjie was the seventh deputy general of the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Xianchun (1274) Anjie was seventh deputy general of the southeast.

sentences.zh: 德祐初，似道潰師蕪湖，列城皆降，不降者亦棄城遁。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Deyou, Sidao's army collapsed at Wuhu. The cities in succession all surrendered; those that did not surrender also abandoned their cities and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Deyou (1275), Sidao's army collapsed at Wuhu. City after city surrendered; those that did not still abandoned their posts and fled.

sentences.zh: 時安節駐兵江陵，即走臨安，上疏乞募兵為捍禦，授閣門祗候、浙西添差兵馬副都監。

translations.literal: At that time Anjie was stationed at Jiangling. He immediately fled to Lin'an, submitted a memorial begging to recruit troops for defense, and was appointed Gate Attendant and additional Vice Director of Troops and Horses in Western Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: Anjie was then stationed at Jiangling. He rushed to Lin'an, memorialized to raise troops for defense, and was made Gate Attendant and additional vice director of Western Zhe military affairs.

sentences.zh: 收兵入平江，合張世傑兵戰鳳皇港，有功，轉三官。

translations.literal: He gathered troops into Pingjiang, joined Zhang Shijie's forces to fight at Fenghuang Harbor, had merit, and was transferred up three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered troops at Pingjiang, joined Zhang Shijie at Fenghuang Harbor, distinguished himself, and advanced three ranks.

sentences.zh: 劉師勇復常州，攻走王良臣，師勇還平江，以安節與張詹守常。

translations.literal: Liu Shiyong recovered Changzhou, attacked and drove off Wang Liangchen, and Shiyong returned to Pingjiang, leaving Anjie and Zhang Zhan to defend Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shiyong retook Changzhou, drove off Wang Liangchen, returned to Pingjiang, and left Anjie and Zhang Zhan to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 已而良臣導大兵攻常，常城素惡，安節等築柵以守，相拒兩月不下。

translations.literal: Before long Liangchen guided the great army to attack Chang. Chang city was by nature difficult, and Anjie and others built palisades to defend. They resisted two months without falling.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liangchen led the main force against Changzhou. The city was naturally strong; Anjie and his men built palisades and held for two months.

sentences.zh: 大元丞相伯顏自將攻之，屢遣使招降，亦不下。

translations.literal: The Great Yuan Chancellor Bayan personally led the attack, repeatedly sent envoys to summon surrender, yet they would not come down.
translations.idiomatic: Great Yuan Chancellor Bayan personally besieged it and repeatedly sent envoys to demand surrender; they still would not yield.

sentences.zh: 丞相怒，麾兵破其南門，安節揮雙刀率死士巷戰，臂傷被執。

translations.literal: The Chancellor was angry and waved the troops to break the south gate. Anjie wielded twin blades and led men willing to die in street fighting. His arm was wounded and he was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the chancellor stormed the south gate. Anjie fought the alleys with twin blades at the head of die-hards until a wounded arm brought him down.

sentences.zh: 有求其姓名者，安節呼曰：“我王堅子安節也。”

translations.literal: When someone asked his name, Anjie shouted, "I am Wang Jian's son Anjie."
translations.idiomatic: When asked his name, Anjie cried, "I am Wang Jian's son, Anjie!"

sentences.zh: 降之不得，乃殺之。

translations.literal: Unable to make him surrender, they then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They could not make him yield, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 尹玉，寧都人。

translations.literal: Yin Yu was a man of Ningdu.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yu came from Ningdu.

sentences.zh: 以捕盜功為贛州三砦巡檢。

translations.literal: For merit in capturing bandits he became inspector of the three stockades of Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For capturing bandits he was made inspector of Ganzhou's three stockades.

sentences.zh: 秩滿城居，從文天祥勤王。

translations.literal: When his term ended he lived in the city and followed Wen Tianxiang in rallying to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he settled in the city and followed Wen Tianxiang to the emperor's aid.

sentences.zh: 及天祥至平江，調玉同淮將張全、廣將朱華拒大兵，戰於伍牧，全等軍敗，以淮、廣軍先遁，曾全、胡遇、謝榮、曾玉以贛州四指揮軍亦遁，唯玉殘軍五百殊死戰。

translations.literal: When Tianxiang reached Pingjiang, Yu was assigned together with the Huai general Zhang Quan and the Guang general Zhu Hua to resist the great army. They fought at Wumu. Quan and the others were defeated. The Huai and Guang armies fled first. Zeng Quan, Hu Yu, Xie Rong, and Zeng Yu with the four command armies of Ganzhou also fled. Only Yu's remnant force of five hundred fought to the death with exceptional valor.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianxiang reached Pingjiang, Yu was sent with Huai general Zhang Quan and Guang general Zhu Hua to hold the main force at Wumu. Quan's army broke; Huai and Guang troops fled first, then Zeng Quan, Hu Yu, Xie Rong, and Zeng Yu with Ganzhou's four command armies. Only Yu's five hundred remnants fought on to the death.

sentences.zh: 玉手殺數十人，箭集於胄如蝟毛，援絕力屈，遂被執。

translations.literal: Yu killed several tens of men with his own hands. Arrows clustered on his helmet like quills. Relief was cut off and strength exhausted, and he was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Yu killed dozens with his own hands. Arrows bristled on his helmet like a hedgehog. Cut off and spent, he was taken.

sentences.zh: 大軍橫四槍於其項，以梃擊之死。

translations.literal: The great army laid four spears across his neck and beat him to death with clubs.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy laid four spears across his neck and beat him to death with clubs.

sentences.zh: 餘兵猶夜戰，殺人馬蔽田間，無一降者。

translations.literal: The remaining troops still fought at night. Men and horses they killed covered the fields. Not one surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: His remaining men fought through the night; dead men and horses covered the fields, and none surrendered.

sentences.zh: 質明，生還者四人。

translations.literal: At first light, four men survived.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn, four men survived.

sentences.zh: 贈玉濠州圍練使，官其二子，賜田二頃，以恤其家。

translations.literal: Yu was posthumously made Prefectural Militia Commissioner of Haozhou, his two sons were given offices, and two qing of fields were granted to comfort his family.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was posthumously made Haozhou militia commissioner; both sons received offices and two qing of land to support the family.

sentences.zh: 李芾，字叔章，其先廣平人，中徙汴。

translations.literal: Li Fei, style name Shuzhang, his ancestors were men of Guangping and midway moved to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fei, styled Shuzhang, came originally from Guangping and later moved to Bian.

sentences.zh: 高祖升起進士，為吏有廉名。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Sheng passed the examinations and as an official had a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Sheng passed the examinations and earned a name for integrity in office.

sentences.zh: 靖康中，金人破汴，以刃迫其父，升前捍之，與父俱死。

translations.literal: In the Jingkang era, when the Jurchens broke Bian, they forced his father with blades. Sheng stepped forward to shield him and died together with his father.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingkang crisis, when the Jurchens took Bian, they threatened his father with blades. Sheng stepped forward to shield him and died with his father.

sentences.zh: 曾祖椿徙家衡州，遂為衡人。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Chun moved the family to Hengzhou and thus became a man of Heng.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Chun moved the family to Hengzhou, and they became Heng natives.

sentences.zh: 芾生而聰警，少自樹立，名其齋曰無暴棄。

translations.literal: Fei was clever and alert from birth. In youth he established himself and named his study No Waste or Abandonment.
translations.idiomatic: Fei was clever from childhood and early made his mark, naming his study No Waste or Abandonment.

sentences.zh: 魏了翁一見禮之，謂有祖風，易其名曰肯齋。

translations.literal: Wei Liaoweng, on first meeting, treated him with courtesy and said he had his ancestor's manner, and changed his name to Willing Studio.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Liaoweng honored him at first meeting, said he bore his ancestors' spirit, and renamed his study Willing Studio.

sentences.zh: 初以蔭補南安司戶，辟祁陽尉，出振荒，即有聲。

translations.literal: At first through yin privilege he was made Nan'an revenue clerk, was summoned as Qiyang assistant magistrate, went out to relieve famine, and at once gained renown.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office by yin privilege as Nan'an revenue clerk, was summoned as Qiyang assistant magistrate, relieved famine, and won immediate renown.

sentences.zh: 攝祁陽縣，縣大治，辟湖南安撫司幕官。

translations.literal: Acting as Qiyang county magistrate, he brought the county to great order and was summoned as staff officer of the Hunan Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Acting magistrate of Qiyang, he brought the county to order and joined the Hunan Pacification Commission staff.

sentences.zh: 時盜起永州，招之，歲餘不下。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose in Yongzhou. They were summoned to surrender, but for more than a year they would not come down.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits rose in Yongzhou; summons to surrender failed for more than a year.

sentences.zh: 芾與參議鄧提千三百人破其巢，禽賊魁蔣時選父子以歸，餘黨遂平。

translations.literal: Fei together with staff adviser Deng led thirteen hundred men to break their lair, captured the bandit chiefs Jiang Shixuan father and son and returned, and the remaining factions were then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Fei and staff adviser Deng led thirteen hundred men, stormed the bandits' lair, captured chiefs Jiang Shixuan and his son, and pacified the rest.

sentences.zh: 攝湘潭縣，縣多大家，前令束手不敢犯。

translations.literal: Acting as Xiangtan county magistrate — the county had many great clans, and the previous magistrate had folded his hands and dared not offend them.
translations.idiomatic: As acting magistrate of Xiangtan — a county of powerful clans whose previous magistrate had dared not touch them.

sentences.zh: 芾稽籍出賦，不避貴勢，賦役大均。

translations.literal: Fei checked the registers and assessed levies, did not avoid noble power, and tax and corvée labor were greatly equalized.
translations.idiomatic: Fei audited registers, assessed levies without fear of powerful families, and equalized taxes and labor.

sentences.zh: 入朝，差知德清縣。

translations.literal: He entered court and was assigned to know Deqing County.
translations.idiomatic: He went to court and was assigned magistrate of Deqing.

sentences.zh: 屬浙西饑，芾置保伍振民，活數萬計。

translations.literal: It happened that Western Zhe suffered famine. Fei established mutual-aid groups to relieve the people and saved several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: When Western Zhe suffered famine, he organized mutual-aid groups and saved tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 遷主管酒庫所。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supervise the Wine Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to oversee the imperial Wine Treasury.

sentences.zh: 德清有妖人扇民為亂，民蜂起附之，至數萬人。

translations.literal: In Deqing a sorcerer incited the people to rebellion. The people swarmed to join him, reaching several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: A sorcerer in Deqing stirred rebellion; tens of thousands flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 遣芾討之，盜聞其來，眾立散歸。

translations.literal: They sent Fei to suppress them. When the rebels heard he was coming, the masses at once scattered and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Fei was sent to suppress them; at word of his coming the rebels dispersed at once.

sentences.zh: 除司農寺丞，曆知永州，有惠政，永人祠之。

translations.literal: He was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue's Agriculture Office, served successively as prefect of Yongzhou, had benevolent administration, and the people of Yong erected a shrine to him.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice director of the Agriculture Office, served as prefect of Yongzhou with benevolent rule, and Yongzhou erected a shrine to him.

sentences.zh: 以浙東提刑知溫州。

translations.literal: As Eastern Zhe investigating censor he was made prefect of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As Eastern Zhe investigating censor he became prefect of Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 州瀕海多盜，芾至盜息，遂以前官移浙西。

translations.literal: The prefecture bordered the sea and had many bandits. When Fei arrived, banditry ceased, and he then moved to Western Zhe in his former capacity.
translations.idiomatic: The coastal prefecture was rife with pirates; when Fei arrived, piracy ceased, and he was transferred to Western Zhe in his former role.

sentences.zh: 時浙西亦多盜，群穴太湖中，芾跡得其出沒按捕之，盜亦駭散。

translations.literal: At that time Western Zhe also had many bandits who clustered in lairs in Lake Tai. Fei traced their movements and arrested them, and the bandits were also terrified and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Western Zhe too swarmed with bandits nesting in Lake Tai. Fei tracked their movements, arrested them, and scattered them in fear.

sentences.zh: 作虎丘書院以祠尹焞，置學官，親為學規以教之，學者甚盛。

translations.literal: He built Tiger Hill Academy to worship Yin Chun, established school officers, and personally made school regulations to teach — scholars flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He founded Tiger Hill Academy to honor Yin Chun, appointed school officers, wrote regulations himself, and drew a great host of students.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳元年，入知臨安府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianchun he entered to serve as prefect of Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianchun (1265) he became prefect of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 時賈似道當國，前尹事無巨細先關白始行，芾獨無所問。

translations.literal: At that time Jia Sidao held the state. The previous prefect, on matters great or small, first reported to Sidao before acting. Fei alone made no such inquiries.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Sidao held power. The previous prefect reported every matter to Sidao before acting; Fei alone did not.

sentences.zh: 福王府有迫人死者，似道力為營救，芾以書往復辨論，竟置諸法。

translations.literal: In the Prince of Fu's mansion someone had been driven to death. Sidao strove to rescue him. Fei argued back and forth in letters and in the end placed him under the law.
translations.idiomatic: Someone died under coercion at the Prince of Fu's mansion. Sidao fought to save him; Fei argued by letter back and forth and in the end had him punished by law.

sentences.zh: 嚐出閱火具，民有不為具者，問之，曰：“似道家人也。”

translations.literal: Once he went out to inspect fire equipment. A man had not provided equipment. When asked, he said, "He is one of Sidao's household."
translations.idiomatic: Once inspecting fire equipment, he found a man who had not supplied his quota. Asked why, the man said, "He is of Sidao's household."

sentences.zh: 立杖之。

translations.literal: He immediately had him beaten with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Fei had him beaten on the spot.

sentences.zh: 似道大怒，使台臣黃萬石誣以贓罪，罷之。

translations.literal: Sidao was greatly angered and had censor Huang Wanshi falsely charge him with corruption and remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao was furious and had censor Huang Wanshi frame him for corruption and remove him from office.

sentences.zh: 大軍取鄂州，始起為湖南提刑。

translations.literal: When the great army took Ezhou, he was first recalled as Hunan investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force took Ezhou, he was recalled as Hunan investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 時郡縣盜擾，民多奔竄，芾令所部發民兵自衛，縣予一皂幟，令曰：“作亂者斬幟下。”

translations.literal: At that time prefectures and counties were disturbed by bandits and the people mostly fled in panic. Fei ordered his subordinates to mobilize militia for self-defense, gave each county one black banner, and proclaimed, "Whoever makes trouble shall be beheaded beneath the banner."
translations.idiomatic: Bandits ravaged the prefectures; people fled in panic. Fei ordered militia mobilized for self-defense, gave each county a black banner, and proclaimed, "Rebels will be beheaded beneath this banner."

sentences.zh: 民始帖然。

translations.literal: The people then became settled.
translations.idiomatic: The people then settled.

sentences.zh: 乃號召發兵，擇壯士三千人，使土豪尹奮忠將之勤王，別召民兵集衡為守備。

translations.literal: He then called up troops, selected three thousand stalwart men, and had the local strongman Yin Fenzhong lead them to rally to the throne. Separately he summoned militia to gather at Heng for defense.
translations.idiomatic: He then raised troops, chose three thousand stalwarts, and sent local leader Yin Fenzhong to the emperor's aid while summoning militia to Heng for defense.

sentences.zh: 未幾，似道兵潰蕪湖，乃復芾官，知潭州兼湖南安撫使。

translations.literal: Before long Sidao's army collapsed at Wuhu, and Fei's office was restored. He was made prefect of Tanzhou and concurrently Hunan Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Sidao's army collapsed at Wuhu. Fei was restored to office as prefect of Tanzhou and Hunan Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時湖北州郡皆已歸附，其友勸芾勿行，曰：“無已，即以身行可也。”

translations.literal: At that time the prefectures and counties of Hubei had all submitted. His friend urged Fei not to go and said, "If you cannot avoid it, then go in person only."
translations.idiomatic: Hubei's prefectures had all submitted. A friend urged Fei not to go: "If you must, go alone at least."

sentences.zh: 芾泣曰：“吾豈昧於謀身哉？

translations.literal: Fei wept and said, "How could I be blind to preserving myself?
translations.idiomatic: Fei wept and said, "Do you think I do not know how to save myself?

sentences.zh: 第以世受國恩，雖廢棄中猶思所以報者，今幸用我，我以家許國矣。”

translations.literal: It is only that our house has received the state's grace for generations. Even in dismissal I still thought how to repay it. Now that I am fortunately employed, I have pledged my family to the state."
translations.idiomatic: Our house has received the state's grace for generations. Even in disgrace I sought how to repay it. Now that I am called, I pledge my family to the realm.

sentences.zh: 時其所愛女死，一慟而行。

translations.literal: At that time his beloved daughter had died. After one burst of grief he set out.
translations.idiomatic: His beloved daughter had just died; he grieved once and set out.

sentences.zh: 大元右丞阿裏海牙既下江陵，分軍戍常德遏諸蠻，而以大兵入潭。

translations.literal: After the Great Yuan Right Chancellor Arighai had taken Jiangling, he divided troops to garrison Changde and block the various Man, and with the great army entered Tan.
translations.idiomatic: After Great Yuan right chancellor Arighai took Jiangling, he garrisoned Changde to hold the tribal frontiers and marched the main force into Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 芾遣其將於興帥兵禦之於湘陰，興戰死。

translations.literal: Fei sent his general Yu Xing to lead troops to resist at Xiangyin. Xing died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Fei sent general Yu Xing to hold Xiangyin; Xing fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 九月，再調繼明出禦，兵不及出，而大軍已圍城。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he again ordered Jiming out to resist, but the troops could not get out in time and the great army had already besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he ordered Jiming out again, but troops could not deploy before the main force had encircled the city.

sentences.zh: 芾慷慨登陴，與諸將分地而守，民老弱亦皆出，結保伍助之，不令而集。

translations.literal: Fei ascended the battlements in high spirit, divided territory with the generals to defend, and the people old and weak also all came out, formed mutual-aid groups to help, and gathered without being ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Fei mounted the walls in high spirit, divided sectors among his generals, and old and young alike came out in mutual-aid groups to help — gathering without command.

sentences.zh: 十月，兵攻西壁，孝忠輩奮戰，芾親冒矢石以督之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the army attacked the west wall. Xiaozhong and his fellows fought fiercely. Fei personally braved arrows and stones to supervise them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the enemy assaulted the west wall. Xiaozhong and his men fought fiercely while Fei braved arrows and stones to direct them.

sentences.zh: 城中矢盡，有故矢皆羽敗，芾命括民間羽扇，羽立具。

translations.literal: In the city arrows were exhausted. There were old arrows whose fletching was ruined. Fei ordered that the people's feather fans be collected, and feathers were at once supplied.
translations.idiomatic: When arrows ran out and old stock had ruined fletching, Fei ordered civilian feather fans collected — feathers were ready at once.

sentences.zh: 又苦食無鹽，芾取庫中積鹽席，焚取鹽給之。

translations.literal: They also suffered from food without salt. Fei took the piled salt mats in the storehouse, burned them to extract salt, and distributed it.
translations.idiomatic: Salt ran short; Fei burned piled salt mats from the storehouse and distributed the salt.

sentences.zh: 有中傷者，躬自撫勞，日以忠義勉其將士。

translations.literal: When men were wounded, he personally comforted and encouraged them, daily exhorting his officers and soldiers with loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He personally comforted the wounded and daily exhorted his men with talk of loyalty and duty.

sentences.zh: 死傷相藉，人猶飲血乘城殊死戰。

translations.literal: The dead and wounded lay upon one another, yet men still drank blood, manned the walls, and fought to the death with exceptional valor.
translations.idiomatic: Dead and wounded lay heaped, yet men still manned the walls and fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 有來招降者，芾殺之以徇。

translations.literal: When anyone came to summon surrender, Fei killed him and displayed the body as warning.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys summoning surrender were killed and displayed as warning.

sentences.zh: 十二月，城圍益急，孝忠中炮，風不能起，諸將泣請曰：“事急矣，吾屬為國死可也，如民何？”

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the siege grew more urgent. Xiaozhong was struck by cannon and could not rise in the wind. The generals wept and pleaded, "The matter is urgent. We may die for the state, but what of the people?"
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the siege tightened. Xiaozhong was struck by cannon and could not rise. Generals wept and pleaded, "Matters are desperate. We can die for the state — but what of the people?"

sentences.zh: 芾罵曰：“國家平時所以厚養汝者，為今日也。

translations.literal: Fei cursed them, saying, "What the state richly nourished you for in normal times was for this day.
translations.idiomatic: Fei cursed them: "The state fed you well in peace for this day alone.

sentences.zh: 汝第死守，有後言者吾先戮汝。”

translations.literal: You need only defend to the death. Whoever speaks afterward, I will execute first."
translations.idiomatic: Hold to the death. Whoever speaks of yielding, I will kill first.

sentences.zh: 除夕，大兵登城，戰少卻，旋蟻附而登，衡守尹穀及其家人自焚，芾命酒酹之。

translations.literal: On New Year's Eve the great army mounted the wall. Fighting briefly fell back, then they swarmed up like ants. Heng prefect Yin Gu and his household burned themselves. Fei ordered wine poured in libation to them.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Eve the enemy scaled the walls, fell back briefly, then swarmed up like ants. Heng prefect Yin Gu and his family burned themselves; Fei poured libations of wine.

sentences.zh: 因留賓佐會飲，夜傳令，猶手書“盡忠”字為號。

translations.literal: He then kept his guests and staff for a drinking gathering, transmitted orders through the night, and still personally wrote the character "Utmost Loyalty" as the signal.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his staff for a final feast, passed orders through the night, and still wrote the signal character Utmost Loyalty by hand.

sentences.zh: 飲達旦，諸賓佐出，參議楊震赴園池死。

translations.literal: They drank until dawn. The guests and staff went out. Staff adviser Yang Zhen went to the garden pool and died.
translations.idiomatic: They drank until dawn. The staff departed; adviser Yang Zhen drowned himself in the garden pool.

sentences.zh: 芾坐熊湘閣召帳下沈忠遺之金曰：“吾力竭，分當死，吾家人亦不可辱於俘，汝盡殺之，而後殺我。”

translations.literal: Fei sat in Xiongxiang Pavilion, summoned his retainer Shen Zhong, and bequeathed him gold, saying, "My strength is spent and by duty I should die. My family also must not suffer the shame of captivity. Kill them all, then kill me."
translations.idiomatic: Fei sat in Xiongxiang Pavilion, summoned retainer Shen Zhong, and gave him gold: "My strength is spent; I must die. My family must not live in shame as captives. Kill them all, then kill me."

sentences.zh: 忠伏地扣頭，辭以不能，芾固命之，忠泣而諾，取酒飲其家人盡醉，乃遍刃之。

translations.literal: Zhong knelt and kowtowed, declining that he could not. Fei firmly commanded him. Zhong wept and assented, took wine and made his family drink until all were drunk, then stabbed them throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong kowtowed and refused, saying he could not. Fei insisted. Zhong wept and agreed, made the family drunk on wine, then stabbed them one by one.

sentences.zh: 芾亦引頸受刃。

translations.literal: Fei also extended his neck to receive the blade.
translations.idiomatic: Fei then offered his neck to the blade.

sentences.zh: 忠縱火焚其居，還家殺其妻子，復至火所，大慟，舉身投地，乃自刎。

translations.literal: Zhong set fire and burned the residence, returned home and killed his wife and children, came again to the fire, wailed greatly, threw his whole body to the ground, and then cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong burned the residence, went home and killed his wife and children, returned to the fire, wailed, threw himself to the ground, and cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 幕屬茶陵顧應焱、安仁陳億孫皆死。

translations.literal: Staff members Gu Yingyan of Chaling and Chen Yisun of Anren also died.
translations.idiomatic: Staff members Gu Yingyan of Chaling and Chen Yisun of Anren also died.

sentences.zh: 潭民聞之，多舉家自盡，城無虛井，縊林木者累累相比。

translations.literal: When the people of Tan heard it, many took their whole households to self-destruction. No well in the city was empty. Those who hanged themselves from trees stood in rows one against another.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, many Tan families destroyed themselves; no well stood empty, and bodies hung from trees in rows.

sentences.zh: 繼明等以城降，陳毅潰圍，將奔閩，中道戰死。

translations.literal: Jiming and others surrendered the city. Chen Yi broke out of the encirclement, intended to flee to Min, and died in battle on the way.
translations.idiomatic: Jiming and others surrendered the city. Chen Yi broke out toward Fujian and died fighting on the road.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈端明殿大學士，諡忠節。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously made Academician of the Duanming Hall and given the posthumous title Zhongjie (Loyal Integrity).
translations.idiomatic: When word reached court, he was posthumously made Duanming Hall academician and titled Loyal Integrity.

sentences.zh: 芾初至潭，遣其子裕孫出，曰：“存汝以奉祀也。”

translations.literal: When Fei first reached Tan, he sent his son Yusun out, saying, "I keep you alive to maintain the sacrifices."
translations.idiomatic: When Fei first reached Tanzhou, he sent out his son Yusun, saying, "I spare you to keep our sacrifices alive."

sentences.zh: 其孫輔叔時亦親迎於溫，皆得不死。

translations.literal: His grandson Fushu at that time was also personally received at Wen and both did not die.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Fushu was likewise received at Wenzhou, and both survived.

sentences.zh: 二王悉詔入閩官之。

translations.literal: The two princes all summoned them into Min and gave them offices.
translations.idiomatic: Both imperial princes summoned them to Fujian and gave them offices.

sentences.zh: 芾為人剛介，不畏強禦，臨事精敏，奸猾不能欺。

translations.literal: Fei as a man was firm and upright, did not fear the powerful, was keen and sharp in handling affairs, and the cunning could not deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Fei was stern and upright by nature, unafraid of the powerful, sharp in affairs, and beyond the reach of fraud.

sentences.zh: 且強力過人，自旦治事至暮無倦色，夜率至三鼓始休，五鼓復起視事。

translations.literal: Moreover his physical strength surpassed others'. From dawn in handling affairs until dusk he showed no weariness. At night he generally worked until the third watch before resting, and at the fifth watch rose again to attend to business.
translations.idiomatic: He was also stronger than most men. He worked from dawn to dusk without tiring; at night he often kept at it until the third watch, rested briefly, and was up again at the fifth watch to resume business.

sentences.zh: 望之凜然猶神明，而好賢禮士，即之溫然，雖一藝小善亦惓惓獎薦之。

translations.literal: Seen from afar he was awe-inspiring like a spirit, yet he loved the worthy and honored scholars; approached, he was warm. Even a small skill or minor merit he earnestly praised and recommended.
translations.idiomatic: At a distance he seemed awesome as a god; up close he was warm toward the worthy and courteous to scholars, and even the smallest talent or virtue he would earnestly praise and recommend.

sentences.zh: 平生居官廉，及擯斥，家無餘貲。

translations.literal: All his life in office he was incorrupt, and when he was dismissed and cast out, the household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He lived incorruptibly in every post, and when he was dismissed and cast aside, his household had nothing left.

sentences.zh: 尹穀，字耕叟，潭州長沙人。

translations.literal: Yin Gu, styled Gengsou, was a man of Changsha in Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Gu, styled Gengsou, was from Changsha in Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 性剛直莊厲，初處郡學，士友皆嚴憚之。

translations.literal: His nature was firm, upright, solemn, and stern. When he first entered the prefectural school, scholar-friends all feared him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He was rigid, upright, and severe by nature. When he first entered the prefectural school, his fellow students all stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 宋以詞賦取士，季年，惟閩、浙賦擅四方。

translations.literal: The Song selected officials through rhapsody and fu prose. In the dynasty's later years, only Fujian and Zhejiang fu prose excelled throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Song recruited officials through rhapsody and fu composition, and in the dynasty's late years only Fujian and Zhejiang dominated that art.

sentences.zh: 穀與同郡刑天榮、董景舒、歐陽逢泰諸人為賦，體裁務為典雅，每一篇出，士爭學之，由是湘賦與閩、浙頡頏。

translations.literal: Gu together with Xing Tianrong, Dong Jingshu, Ouyang Fengtai, and others of the same commandery wrote fu prose, striving in form and style for elegance and refinement. Whenever a piece appeared, scholars vied to study it. From this Hunan fu prose matched Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Gu and fellow Hunan writers such as Xing Tianrong, Dong Jingshu, and Ouyang Fengtai composed fu in a deliberately elegant style. Each new piece set scholars scrambling to imitate it, until Hunan fu could stand beside the Fujian and Zhejiang schools.

sentences.zh: 中年登進士第。

translations.literal: In middle age he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in middle age.

sentences.zh: 調常德推官，知崇陽縣，所至廉正有聲。

translations.literal: He was assigned as investigating magistrate of Changde and served as magistrate of Chongyang County. Wherever he went he was known for integrity and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: He served as investigating magistrate in Changde and as magistrate of Chongyang County, earning a reputation for integrity wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，居家教授，不改儒素。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother, stayed home to teach, and did not change his plain Confucian ways.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he stayed home to teach and lived as plainly as ever.

sentences.zh: 日未出，授諸生經及朱氏《四書》，士雖有才思而不謹飭者擯不齒。

translations.literal: Before the sun rose he lectured students on the classics and Zhu Xi's Four Books. Scholars who had talent and thought but were not disciplined and proper he cast out and would not count among his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn he taught the classics and Zhu Xi's Four Books. Talented but undisciplined students he expelled and refused to count among his pupils.

sentences.zh: 諸生隆暑必盛服，端居終日，夜滅燭始免巾幘，早作必冠而後出帷。

translations.literal: Students in the height of summer had to wear full dress, sit upright all day, and only when the candles were extinguished at night might they remove cap and headcloth. When they rose early they had to put on caps before leaving the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: Even in midsummer his students wore full dress and sat upright all day, removing caps and headcloths only after the candles were put out at night, and putting on caps again before leaving their quarters at dawn.

sentences.zh: 行市中，市人見其舉動有禮，相謂曰：“是必尹先生門人也。”

translations.literal: Walking in the market, townspeople seeing their conduct was courteous said to one another, "These must be disciples of Master Yin."
translations.idiomatic: In the marketplace people would see their courteous bearing and say to one another, "Those must be Master Yin's students."

sentences.zh: 詰人果然。

translations.literal: Questioning them, it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: And when questioned, it always proved true.

sentences.zh: 晚入李庭芝製幕，用薦擢知衡州，需次於家。

translations.literal: In his later years he entered the staff of Li Tingzhi's military commission. Through recommendation he was promoted to prefect of Hengzhou and awaited his turn at home.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Li Tingzhi's military commission staff, was recommended for promotion to prefect of Hengzhou, and was waiting at home for his appointment.

sentences.zh: 潭城受兵，帥臣李芾禮以為參謀，共畫備禦策。

translations.literal: When Tan city came under attack, the commander Li Fei honored him and made him a staff adviser, and together they devised plans for defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Tanzhou came under siege, commander Li Fei honored him with a staff post as adviser, and together they planned the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 時城中壯士皆入衛臨安，所餘軍僅四百五十人，老弱太半。

translations.literal: At that time the city's able-bodied men had all gone to guard Lin'an. The remaining troops numbered only four hundred fifty, more than half of them old or weak.
translations.idiomatic: By then the city's able-bodied men had all gone to defend Lin'an. Only four hundred fifty soldiers remained, more than half of them old or infirm.

sentences.zh: 芾糾率民丁，獎勵以義，人殊死戰，三月城不下。

translations.literal: Fei mustered the civilian militia, encouraged them with righteousness, and men fought to the death. For three months the city did not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Fei mustered the militia, roused them with appeals to duty, and they fought as if death meant nothing; for three months the city held.

sentences.zh: 大軍斷絕險要，援兵不至，穀知城危，與妻子訣曰：“吾以寒儒受國恩，典方州，誼不可屈，若輩必當從吾已耳。”

translations.literal: The great army cut off the strategic passes and relief troops did not arrive. Gu knew the city was in peril. He took leave of his wife and children, saying, "I, a humble scholar, have received the state's grace and govern a prefecture. Righteous duty cannot bend. You must follow me in this, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: The main force sealed the strategic passes and no relief came. Seeing the city doomed, Gu bade farewell to his wife and children: "I am only a humble scholar who received the state's favor and was entrusted with a prefecture. Duty cannot bend — you must follow me in this."

sentences.zh: 召弟嶽秀使出，以存尹氏祀，嶽秀泣而許之死。

translations.literal: He summoned his younger brother Yue Xiu and sent him out to preserve the Yin clan sacrifices. Yue Xiu wept and promised to die.
translations.idiomatic: He sent out his younger brother Yue Xiu to preserve the Yin line. Yue Xiu wept and vowed to die with the rest.

sentences.zh: 乃積薪扃戶，朝服望闕拜已，先取曆官告身焚之，即縱火自焚。

translations.literal: Then he piled firewood, barred the door, put on court dress, bowed toward the palace, took out the appointment documents from his successive offices and burned them, and then set the fire and burned himself.
translations.idiomatic: He piled firewood, barred the door, put on court dress, bowed toward the capital, burned his appointment documents from every post he had held, and set himself ablaze.

sentences.zh: 鄰家救之，火熾不可前，但於烈焰中遙見穀正冠端笏危坐，闔門無少長皆死焉。

translations.literal: Neighbors tried to save them, but the fire was fierce and none could advance. They could only see from afar in the flames Gu wearing his cap straight, holding his tablet properly, sitting upright in peril, and the whole household, young and old alike, all died.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors tried to rescue them, but the flames were too fierce to approach. Through the blaze they could only see Gu seated upright in full cap and tablet, and every member of the household, young and old, perished.

sentences.zh: 芾聞之，命酒酹穀曰：“尹務實，男子也，先我就義矣。”

translations.literal: When Fei heard it, he ordered wine poured as libation to Gu and said, "Yin Wushi — a true man — has gone to his death before me."
translations.idiomatic: When Fei heard, he poured wine as an offering and said, "Yin Wushi — what a man — has died for the cause before me."

sentences.zh: 務實，穀號也。

translations.literal: Wushi was Gu's sobriquet.
translations.idiomatic: Wushi was Gu's sobriquet.

sentences.zh: 初，潭士以居學肄業為重，州學生月試積分高等，升湘西嶽麓書院生，又積分高等，升嶽麓精舍生，潭人號為“三學生”。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tan scholars regarded residence study as important. Prefectural school students who in monthly examinations accumulated high scores advanced to students of the Yuelu Academy in western Hunan; accumulating high scores again, they advanced to students of the Yuelu Seminary. The people of Tan called them "three-tier students."
translations.idiomatic: Tan scholars had long prized residential study. Prefectural students who scored highest in monthly exams advanced to the Yuelu Academy in western Hunan; top scorers there advanced again to the Yuelu Seminary — a progression Tan people called the "three-tier students."

sentences.zh: 兵興時，三學生聚居州學，猶不廢業。

translations.literal: When war arose, the three-tier students gathered and lived together at the prefectural school and still did not abandon their studies.
translations.idiomatic: Even when war broke out, the three-tier students gathered at the prefectural school and never abandoned their studies.

sentences.zh: 穀死，諸生數百人往哭之，城破，多感激死義者。

translations.literal: When Gu died, several hundred students went to mourn him. When the city fell, many were moved and died for righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When Gu died, hundreds of his students came to mourn him. After the city fell, many were so moved that they died for the cause.

sentences.zh: 楊霆，字震仲。

translations.literal: Yang Ting, styled Zhenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ting, styled Zhenzhong.

sentences.zh: 少有志節。

translations.literal: From youth he had resolve and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a youth he showed resolve and integrity.

sentences.zh: 以世澤奏補將仕郎，銓試第一，授修職郎、桂嶺主簿，有能聲。

translations.literal: Through hereditary privilege he was memorialized and appointed Gentleman for Official Service. He ranked first in the appointment examination and was given the posts of Cultivated Duty Gentleman and chief clerk of Guiling, and gained a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he entered service as Gentleman for Official Service, ranked first in the appointment examination, and was made Cultivated Duty Gentleman and chief clerk of Guiling, quickly earning a name for competence.

sentences.zh: 又五中漕舉，改鄂州教授，遷復州司理參軍，轉常、澧觀察推官，擢知監利縣。

translations.literal: He also passed the transport commission examination five times, was transferred to instructor at Ezhou, moved to judicial aide of Fuzhou, became investigating magistrate under the Chang and Li observation commission, and was promoted to magistrate of Jianli County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the transport commission examination five times, served as instructor at Ezhou, then as judicial aide in Fuzhou, investigating magistrate under the Chang-Li observation commission, and was finally promoted to magistrate of Jianli County.

sentences.zh: 縣有疑獄，曆年不決，霆未上，微服廉得其實，立決之，人稱神明。

translations.literal: The county had a doubtful case that for years had not been decided. Before Ting had taken office, he went in disguise to investigate and obtained the truth, immediately decided it, and people called him divine.
translations.idiomatic: The county had a doubtful case unresolved for years. Before even taking office, Ting went in disguise to investigate, learned the truth, settled it at once, and people hailed him as uncannily just.

sentences.zh: 辟荊湖製置司幹官。

translations.literal: He was recruited as a staff officer of the Jinghu Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was recruited as a staff officer on the Jinghu Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 呂文德為帥，素慢侮士，常試以難事，霆倉卒立辦，皆合其意。

translations.literal: Lü Wende was commander and habitually looked down on and insulted scholars. He often tested them with difficult tasks. Ting at once handled them and all matched his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Lü Wende habitually looked down on scholars and often tested them with hard tasks. Ting handled each one on the spot to Wende's satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 一日謂曰：“朝廷有密旨，出師策應淮東，誰可往者？”

translations.literal: One day he said to him, "The court has a secret order to march out and coordinate with Huaidong. Who can go?"
translations.idiomatic: One day Wende asked him, "The court has a secret order to march and support Huaidong. Who should go?"

sentences.zh: 即對曰某將可。

translations.literal: He immediately replied that a certain general would do.
translations.idiomatic: Ting immediately named a suitable general.

sentences.zh: 又曰：“兵器糧草若何？”

translations.literal: He again said, "What of weapons, grain, and fodder?"
translations.idiomatic: Wende asked again, "What about arms, grain, and fodder?"

sentences.zh: 即對曰某營兵馬、某庫器甲、某處矢石、某處芻糧，口占授吏，頃刻案成。

translations.literal: He immediately replied: such-and-such camp's troops and horses, such-and-such storehouse's armor, such-and-such place's arrows and stones, such-and-such place's hay and grain — dictating to clerks, in a moment the documents were complete.
translations.idiomatic: Ting answered at once — which camp's troops and horses, which depot's armor, which stockpiles of arrows and stones, which stores of hay and grain — dictating to clerks until the papers were finished in moments.

sentences.zh: 文德大驚曰：“吾平生輕文人，以其不事事也。

translations.literal: Wende was greatly startled and said, "All my life I have looked lightly on literati because they attend to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Wende was astonished. "All my life I have scorned literati as men who attend to nothing,

sentences.zh: 公材幹如此，何官不可為，吾何敢不敬。”

translations.literal: Your talent and capacity are like this — what office could you not hold? How would I dare not respect you?"
translations.idiomatic: yet your capacity is such that no office is beyond you. How could I fail to respect you?"

sentences.zh: 密薦諸朝，除通判江陵府。

translations.literal: He secretly recommended him to the court, and Ting was appointed vice-prefect of Jiangling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly recommended him to court, and Ting was appointed vice-prefect of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 江陵大府，雄據上流，表裏襄、漢，西控巴蜀，南扼湖、廣。

translations.literal: Jiangling was a great prefecture, powerfully holding the upper reaches, with Xiang and Han within and without, controlling Ba and Shu to the west and blocking Hunan and Guang to the south.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangling was a great prefecture commanding the upper Yangtze, flanked by the Xiang and Han rivers, holding Ba-Shu to the west and guarding Hunan and Guangdong to the south.

sentences.zh: 兵民雜處，庶務叢集，霆隨事裁決，處之泰然。

translations.literal: Soldiers and civilians lived mixed together and miscellaneous affairs piled up. Ting decided matters as they came and handled them with calm ease.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and civilians lived side by side and business piled up endlessly, yet Ting decided each matter as it arose with unflappable calm.

sentences.zh: 暇日詣郡庠，與諸生講學，又取隸官閑田，增益廩稍。

translations.literal: On free days he went to the prefectural school and lectured with the students. He also took idle land belonging to subordinate offices and increased grain stipends.
translations.idiomatic: In his spare time he lectured at the prefectural school, took idle land from subordinate offices, and increased students' grain stipends.

sentences.zh: 選民之強壯，當農隙訓練之，時付以器械，雜兵行肄習，親閱試行賞以激勸之。

translations.literal: He selected strong civilians and, during gaps in farm work, trained them, at times supplying them with weapons, mixing them with soldiers in drill, personally reviewing and testing them and giving rewards to encourage them.
translations.idiomatic: He selected able-bodied civilians, drilled them between planting seasons, armed them, mixed them with regular troops in training, personally inspected them, and rewarded performance to spur them on.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有能擐甲騎射者，遂皆獲其用，而兵不復擾民。

translations.literal: Before long there were men able to don armor and shoot from horseback. All were put to use, and soldiers no longer harassed the people.
