translations.idiomatic: Before long he had men who could don armor and shoot from horseback, all of them put to good use, and soldiers no longer harassed the populace.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，德祐初，起復奉議郎、湖南安撫司參議，與安撫使李芾協力戰守。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother. At the beginning of the Deyou reign he was recalled from mourning as Proposal-Discussing Gentleman and deliberative officer of the Hunan Pacification Commission, and together with Pacification Commissioner Li Fei exerted joint effort in fighting and defense.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his mother he was recalled early in the Deyou era as Proposal-Discussing Gentleman and deliberative officer on the Hunan Pacification Commission, where he joined Pacification Commissioner Li Fei in the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 霆有心計，善出奇應變，帥府機務，芾一以委之。

translations.literal: Ting had resourceful plans, was good at unexpected responses to changing situations, and Fei entrusted all the commander's confidential affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ting was resourceful and skilled at improvising under pressure, and Fei entrusted all headquarters business to him.

sentences.zh: 城初被圍，日夜守禦，數日西北隅破，霆麾兵巷戰，抵暮增築月城，比旦城復完，策厲將士，以死守之。

translations.literal: When the city was first besieged, day and night they defended. After several days the northwest corner was breached. Ting commanded troops in street fighting, and by evening added construction to the barbican. By dawn the wall was restored complete. He urged and encouraged officers and soldiers to defend it to the death.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege began he defended day and night. After several days the northwest corner broke; Ting led street fighting, rebuilt the barbican overnight, and by dawn the wall was whole again. He rallied the garrison to hold to the death.

sentences.zh: 城既破，霆赴水死，妻妾奔救無及，遂皆死。

translations.literal: When the city had fallen, Ting went into the water and died. His wife and concubines ran to save him but could not reach him in time, and so all died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Ting drowned himself. His wife and concubines rushed to save him but could not reach him in time, and all perished.

sentences.zh: 趙卯發，字漢卿，昌州人。

translations.literal: Zhao Maofa, styled Hanqing, was a man of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Maofa, styled Hanqing, was from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 淳祐十年，以上舍登第，為遂寧府司戶、潼川簽判、宣城宰。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chunyou he passed the examinations as an upper dormitory student and served as revenue recorder of Suining Prefecture, signing clerk of Tongchuan, and magistrate of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Chunyou he passed the examinations from the upper dormitory and served as revenue recorder in Suining Prefecture, signing clerk in Tongchuan, and magistrate of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 素以節行稱。

translations.literal: He was always known for integrity of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been known for integrity.

sentences.zh: 中被論罷。

translations.literal: Midway he was impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-career he was impeached and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 咸淳七年，起為彭澤令。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xianchun he was recalled and made magistrate of Pengze.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xianchun he was recalled as magistrate of Pengze.

sentences.zh: 十年，權通判池州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he served as acting vice-prefect of Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he served as acting vice-prefect of Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 大兵渡江，池守王起宗棄官去，卯發攝州事，繕壁聚糧，為守禦計。

translations.literal: When the great army crossed the Yangtze, Chizhou prefect Wang Qizong abandoned his office and fled. Maofa took charge of prefectural affairs, repaired the walls, gathered grain, and planned for defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force crossed the Yangtze, Prefect Wang Qizong abandoned his post and fled. Maofa took charge of the prefecture, repaired the walls, stockpiled grain, and prepared to defend.

sentences.zh: 夏貴兵敗歸，所過縱掠，卯發捕斬十餘人，兵乃戢。

translations.literal: Xia Gui's army returned defeated and along the way plundered at will. Maofa arrested and executed more than ten men, and the soldiers then restrained themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia Gui's defeated army passed through looting freely, Maofa arrested and executed more than ten men, and the troops finally quieted down.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，大兵至李王河，都統張林屢諷之降，卯發忿氣填膺，瞠目視林不能言。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year the great army reached the Li-Wang River. Commander-in-chief Zhang Lin repeatedly hinted that he should surrender. Maofa's breast filled with indignant rage; he stared wide-eyed at Lin and could not speak.
translations.idiomatic: The following first month the main force reached the Li-Wang River. Commander Zhang Lin repeatedly hinted that he should surrender. Maofa burned with indignation, stared at Lin with bulging eyes, and could not speak.

sentences.zh: 有問以禔身之道者，卯發曰：“忠義所以禔身也，此外非臣子所得言。”

translations.literal: When someone asked about the way to preserve one's person, Maofa said, "Loyalty and righteousness are how one preserves one's person. Beyond that is nothing a subject and son may speak of."
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked how to preserve one's integrity, Maofa said, "Loyalty and righteousness are how one preserves one's person — beyond that a subject has nothing to say."

sentences.zh: 林以兵出巡江，陰降，歸而陽助卯發為守，守兵五百餘，柄皆歸林。

translations.literal: Lin took troops out to patrol the river, secretly surrendered, and on returning openly helped Maofa in defense. The defending troops numbered more than five hundred, but all authority fell to Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Lin marched out to patrol the river, secretly submitted, then returned pretending to help Maofa defend. The garrison numbered just over five hundred, but real power rested entirely with Lin.

sentences.zh: 卯發知不可守，乃置酒會親友，與飲訣，謂其妻雍氏曰：“城將破，吾守臣不當去，汝先出走。”

translations.literal: Maofa knew the city could not be held. He set out wine, gathered kin and friends, drank farewell with them, and said to his wife Lady Yong, "The city is about to fall. As defending official I ought not leave. You go out first."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the city could not hold, Maofa held a farewell feast for kin and friends and told his wife Lady Yong, "The city will fall. As its defender I cannot leave — you should escape first."

sentences.zh: 雍氏曰：“君為命官，我為命婦，君為忠臣，我獨不能為忠臣婦乎？”

translations.literal: Lady Yong said, "You are an appointed official; I am an official's wife. You would be a loyal minister — can I alone not be a loyal minister's wife?"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yong replied, "You hold an official commission and I am an official's wife. If you will be a loyal minister, why should I not be a loyal minister's wife?"

sentences.zh: 卯發笑曰：“此豈婦人女子之所能也。”

translations.literal: Maofa smiled and said, "How could this be within the capacity of women and girls?"
translations.idiomatic: Maofa smiled and said, "That is hardly what wives and daughters are expected to do."

sentences.zh: 雍氏曰：“吾請先君死。”

translations.literal: Lady Yong said, "I ask to die before you, my lord."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yong said, "Then let me die before you."

sentences.zh: 卯發笑止之。

translations.literal: Maofa smiled and stopped her.
translations.idiomatic: Maofa smiled and dissuaded her.

sentences.zh: 明日乃散其家資與其弟侄，仆婢悉遣之。

translations.literal: The next day he distributed his household wealth to his younger brothers and nephews and sent away all servants male and female.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he divided his household goods among his brothers and nephews and dismissed every servant.

sentences.zh: 二月，兵薄池，卯發晨起書幾上曰：“君不可叛，城不可降，夫妻同死，節義成雙。”

translations.literal: In the second month the army pressed close to Chi. Maofa rose in the morning and wrote on the table, "The lord must not betray; the city must not surrender. Husband and wife die together — integrity and righteousness made a pair."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the enemy closed on Chizhou. Maofa wrote on his desk that morning: "The lord must not betray, the city must not surrender — husband and wife die together, integrity paired in death."

sentences.zh: 又為詩別其兄弟，與雍盛服同縊從容堂死。

translations.literal: He also composed poems to take leave of his brothers, and with Lady Yong in full dress together hanged themselves in the Hall of Composed Ease and died.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote farewell poems to his brothers, then he and Lady Yong, both in full dress, hanged themselves together in the Hall of Composed Ease.

sentences.zh: 卯發始為此堂，名“可以從容”，及兵遽，領客堂中，指所題扁曰：“吾必死於是。”

translations.literal: When Maofa first built this hall he named it "One May Be at Ease." When war came suddenly, he led guests into the hall, pointed to the inscribed plaque, and said, "I shall surely die here."
translations.idiomatic: When Maofa first built the hall he had named it "One May Be at Ease." When war came suddenly he led guests inside, pointed to the inscribed plaque, and said, "I shall surely die here."

sentences.zh: 客問其故，曰：“古人謂‘慷慨殺身易，從容就義難”，此殆其兆也。”

translations.literal: The guests asked the reason. He said, "The ancients said, 'It is easy to die impulsively; it is hard to meet death with composure.' This is probably its omen."
translations.idiomatic: When they asked why, he said, "The ancients said, 'It is easy to die in a burst of passion; it is hard to meet death with composure.' This name was the sign."

sentences.zh: 卯發死，林開門降。

translations.literal: After Maofa died, Lin opened the gate and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: After Maofa died, Lin opened the gates and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 大元丞相伯顏入，問太守何在，左右以死對。

translations.literal: Great Yuan Chancellor Bayan entered and asked where the prefect was. Those beside him answered that he was dead.
translations.idiomatic: Great Yuan chancellor Bayan entered and asked where the prefect was. His attendants answered that he was dead.

sentences.zh: 即如堂中觀之，皆歎息。

translations.literal: He at once went to the hall to view them. All sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan went at once to the hall to see for himself, and all who looked sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 為具棺衾合葬於池上，祭其墓而去。

translations.literal: He had coffins and shrouds prepared, buried them together on the hill above Chi, sacrificed at their tomb, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He provided coffins and shrouds, buried them together on the hill above Chizhou, offered sacrifice at their tomb, and departed.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈華文閣待制，諡文節，雍氏贈順義夫人，錄二子為京官。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Maofa was posthumously made Attendant Drafting Gentleman of the Huawen Pavilion and given the posthumous title Wenjie (Cultured Integrity). Lady Yong was posthumously made Lady Shunyi (Obedient Righteousness), and their two sons were enrolled as capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached court, Maofa was posthumously made Huawen Pavilion attendant drafting gentleman with the posthumous title Cultured Integrity; Lady Yong was made Lady Obedient Righteousness, and their two sons were enrolled as capital officials.

sentences.zh: 唐震，字景實，會稽人。

translations.literal: Tang Zhen, styled Jingshi, was a man of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zhen, styled Jingshi, was from Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 少居鄉，介然不苟交，有言其過者輒喜。

translations.literal: In youth while living in the countryside he was upright and would not associate casually. When someone spoke of his faults he was always pleased.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man in the countryside he was upright and would not associate casually with others, yet he was always pleased when someone pointed out his faults.

sentences.zh: 既登第為小官，有權貴以牒薦之者，震內牒篋中，已而幹政，震取牒還之，封題未啟，其人大愧。

translations.literal: After passing the examinations and serving as a minor official, a powerful noble sent a memorial recommending him. Zhen put the memorial in his document case. Later when that man came to intervene in affairs, Zhen took out the memorial and returned it — the seal and address had not been opened — and the man was greatly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: After entering office as a minor official, a powerful man sent him a recommendation. Zhen filed it unopened. When the man later came seeking favors, Zhen returned the sealed memorial untouched, to the man's deep shame.

sentences.zh: 後為他官，所至以公廉稱。

translations.literal: Later in other offices, wherever he went he was known for fairness and incorruptibility.
translations.idiomatic: In later posts he was known everywhere for fairness and integrity.

sentences.zh: 楊棟、葉夢鼎居政府，交薦其賢。

translations.literal: Yang Dong and Ye Mengding held positions in the central government and together recommended his worth.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dong and Ye Mengding, then in the central government, jointly recommended his merit.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳中，由大理司直通判臨安府。

translations.literal: During Xianchun he passed through the Court of Judicial Review and was made vice-prefect of Lin'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianchun era he rose through the Court of Judicial Review to vice-prefect of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 時潛說友尹京，恃賈似道勢，甚驕蹇，政事一切無所顧讓。

translations.literal: At that time Qian Shuoyou governed the capital, relying on Jia Sidao's power. He was very arrogant and overbearing, and in all affairs gave way to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Qian Shuoyou governed the capital backed by Jia Sidao's power. He was insufferably arrogant and brooked no restraint in anything he did.

sentences.zh: 會府有具獄將置辟，震力辨其非，說友爭之不得，上其事刑部，卒是震議。

translations.literal: It happened that the prefecture had a completed case about to be sent for execution. Zhen forcefully argued its error. Shuoyou disputed but could not prevail, reported the matter to the Ministry of Justice, and in the end Zhen's view was upheld.
translations.idiomatic: When the prefecture had a completed case ready for execution, Zhen forcefully argued it was wrong. Shuoyou could not prevail, appealed to the Ministry of Justice, and in the end Zhen's view was upheld.

sentences.zh: 六年，江東大旱，擢知信州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, with eastern Jiang suffering great drought, he was promoted to prefect of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, amid severe drought in eastern Jiang, he was promoted to prefect of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 震奏減綱運米，蠲其租賦，令坊置一吏，籍其戶，勸富人分粟，使坊吏主給之。

translations.literal: Zhen memorialized to reduce tribute grain shipped by quota, remitted rents and levies, ordered each ward to appoint one clerk to register its households, urged the wealthy to share grain, and had ward clerks take charge of distribution.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen memorialized to cut tribute grain shipments and remit rents and levies, ordered each ward to appoint a clerk to register households, urged the wealthy to share grain, and put ward clerks in charge of distribution.

sentences.zh: 吏有勞者，輒為具奏復其身，吏感其誠，事為盡力，所活無算。

translations.literal: Clerks who had labored he always memorialized in detail to restore their personal status. The clerks were moved by his sincerity and served with full effort. Those saved were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to restore the personal status of clerks who had served well. Moved by his sincerity, they worked with all their strength, and countless lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 州有民庸童牧牛，童逸而牧舍火，其父訟庸者殺其子投火中，民不勝掠，自誣服。

translations.literal: In the prefecture a man hired a boy to herd cattle. The boy ran off and the cattle shed caught fire. The father sued the hirer, saying he had killed his son and thrown him into the fire. The man could not endure the beating and falsely confessed.
translations.idiomatic: A man hired a boy to herd cattle; the boy ran off and the cattle shed burned. The father sued the hirer, claiming he had killed the boy and thrown him into the fire. Unable to bear the beating, the man falsely confessed.

sentences.zh: 震視牘疑之，密物色之，得童傍郡，以詰其父，對如初，震出其子示之，獄遂直。

translations.literal: Zhen looked at the documents and doubted the case. Secretly he searched for the boy and found him in a neighboring commandery. He questioned the father, who answered as before. Zhen produced the son and showed him, and the case was straightened.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen read the file and was suspicious. He secretly tracked down the boy in a neighboring commandery, questioned the father, who stuck to his story, then produced the living son — and the case was cleared.

sentences.zh: 擢浙西提刑。

translations.literal: He was promoted to judicial intendant of western Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to judicial intendant of western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 過闕陛辭，似道以類田屬震，震謝不能行，至部，又以疏力爭之。

translations.literal: Passing the palace for audience on farewell, Sidao entrusted Leitian land to Zhen. Zhen declined, saying he could not carry it out. Reaching his post, he again memorialized forcefully disputing it.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience Sidao assigned him Leitian land. Zhen declined, saying he could not do it, and after reaching his post memorialized forcefully against the order.

sentences.zh: 趙氏有守阡僧甚暴橫，震遣吏捕治，似道以書營救，震不省，卒按以法。

translations.literal: The Zhao clan had a tomb-guarding monk who was very violent and overbearing. Zhen sent clerks to arrest and punish him. Sidao wrote a letter to intercede. Zhen paid no heed and in the end prosecuted him according to law.
translations.idiomatic: A Zhao clan tomb-guarding monk was notoriously brutal. Zhen sent officers to arrest him. Sidao wrote to intercede, but Zhen ignored the plea and prosecuted the monk to the full extent of the law.

sentences.zh: 似道怒，使侍御史陳堅劾去之。

translations.literal: Sidao was angry and had Remonstrating Censor Chen Jian impeach and remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao, enraged, had remonstrating censor Chen Jian impeach and remove him.

sentences.zh: 咸淳十年，起震知饒州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianchun, Zhen was recalled and made prefect of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Xianchun, Zhen was recalled as prefect of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 時興國、南康、江州諸郡皆已歸附，大兵略饒。

translations.literal: At that time the prefectures of Xingguo, Nankang, Jiangzhou, and others had all submitted. The great army overran Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: By then Xingguo, Nankang, Jiangzhou, and neighboring prefectures had all submitted, and the main force was closing on Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 饒兵止千八百人，震發州民城守，昧爽出治兵，至夜中始寐，上書求援，不報。

translations.literal: Raozhou's troops numbered only one thousand eight hundred. Zhen mobilized the prefecture's people to defend the walls. At dawn he went out to drill troops and did not sleep until midnight. He memorialized seeking relief but received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Raozhou had only eighteen hundred soldiers. Zhen mobilized the populace to man the walls, drilled troops from dawn until midnight, and memorialized for relief — but no answer came.

sentences.zh: 大兵使人入饒取降款，通判萬道同陰使於所部斂白金、牛酒備降禮，饒寓士皆從之。

translations.literal: The great army sent men into Raozhou to obtain a surrender document. Vice-prefect Wan Daotong secretly had his subordinates collect white gold, cattle, and wine to prepare surrender gifts. Gentry residing in Raozhou all followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy sent envoys to Raozhou for a surrender document. Vice-prefect Wan Daotong secretly ordered his subordinates to collect silver, cattle, and wine for surrender gifts, and local gentry went along.

sentences.zh: 道同風震降，震叱之曰：“我忍偷生負國邪？”

translations.literal: Daotong urged Zhen to surrender. Zhen rebuked him, saying, "Could I bear to cling to life and betray the state?"
translations.idiomatic: Daotong pressed Zhen to surrender. Zhen rebuked him: "Do you think I would cling to life and betray the realm?"

sentences.zh: 城中少年感震言，殺使者。

translations.literal: The city's young men, moved by Zhen's words, killed the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Stirred by Zhen's words, the city's young men killed the envoys.

sentences.zh: 民有李希聖者謀出降，械置獄中。

translations.literal: Among the people was one Li Xisheng who plotted to go out and surrender. He was shackled and placed in prison.
translations.idiomatic: A townsman named Li Xisheng plotted to surrender; Zhen had him shackled and jailed.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，兵大至，都大提舉鄧益遁去，震盡出府中金錢，書官資揭於城，募有能出戰者賞之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year the army came in great force. The overall intendant Deng Yi fled. Zhen brought out all the gold and cash in the prefectural treasury, posted office ranks and rewards on the wall, and recruited anyone able to go out and fight, rewarding them.
translations.idiomatic: The next February the main force arrived. Overall intendant Deng Yi fled. Zhen emptied the treasury, posted ranks and rewards on the walls, and paid anyone willing to fight.

sentences.zh: 眾懼不能戰，北兵登陴，眾遂潰。

translations.literal: The masses feared they could not fight. The Northern Army mounted the battlements, and the masses then collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The people feared they could not hold. The northerners scaled the walls, and the defense broke.

sentences.zh: 震入府中玉芝堂，其仆前請曰：“事急矣，番江門兵未合，亟出猶可免。”

translations.literal: Zhen entered the Jade Mushroom Hall in the prefectural compound. His servant stepped forward and pleaded, "The matter is urgent. The troops at Fanjiang Gate are not yet joined — hurry out and you may still escape."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen withdrew to the Jade Mushroom Hall in the yamen. His servant pleaded, "Matters are desperate — troops at Fanjiang Gate are not yet closed in. Leave now and you may yet escape."

sentences.zh: 震罵曰：“城中民命皆係於我，我若從爾言得不死，城中民死，我何面目生邪？”

translations.literal: Zhen cursed him, saying, "The lives of the people in the city all depend on me. If I follow your words and do not die, yet the people in the city die — with what face could I live?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhen cursed him: "The city's people depend on me. If I flee and live while they die, how could I show my face again?"

sentences.zh: 左右不復敢言，皆出。

translations.literal: Those at his side no longer dared speak and all went out.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants dared say no more and left.

sentences.zh: 有頃，兵入，執牘鋪案上，使震署降，震擲筆於地，不屈，遂死之。

translations.literal: Before long the soldiers entered, placed a document on the desk, and made Zhen sign the surrender. Zhen threw the brush to the ground, would not submit, and was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon soldiers entered, laid a surrender document before him, and demanded his signature. Zhen threw the brush down, refused to yield, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 兄椿與家人俱死。

translations.literal: His elder brother Chun and the whole household also died.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Chun and the entire household died as well.

sentences.zh: 張世傑尋復饒州，判官鄔宗節求震屍葬之。

translations.literal: Zhang Shijie soon recovered Raozhou. Vice-prefect Wu Zongjie sought out Zhen's corpse and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shijie soon retook Raozhou; vice-prefect Wu Zongjie recovered Zhen's body and buried it.

sentences.zh: 贈華文閣待制，諡忠介，廟號褒忠，官其二子。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Huawen Attendant-in-Waiting, given the posthumous title Zhongjie (Loyal and Upright), temple name Bao Zhong (Commending Loyalty), and his two sons were given offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Huawen Attendant-in-Waiting, titled Loyal and Upright, shrine named Commending Loyalty, and both sons received offices.

sentences.zh: 震客馮驥、何新之，驥後守獨鬆關，新之守閩之新壘，皆戰死。

translations.literal: Zhen's clients Feng Ji and He Xinzhi — Ji later defended Dusong Pass and Xinzhi defended Xinlei in Min — both died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's clients Feng Ji and He Xinzhi later held Dusong Pass and Fujian's Xinlei fort respectively; both died fighting.

sentences.zh: 趙與檡，為嗣秀王。

translations.literal: Zhao Yushi was the heir to the Prince of Xiù.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yushi was heir to the Prince of Xiù.

sentences.zh: 德祐二年，為浙、閩、廣察訪使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Deyou he was made Investigating Commissioner for Zhe, Min, and Guang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Deyou (1276) he was made investigating commissioner for Zhe, Fujian, and Guang.

sentences.zh: 益王之立，舅楊亮節居中秉權，與檡自以國家親賢，多所諫止，遂犯忌嫉，諸將俱憚之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yi was established, his maternal uncle Yang Liangjie held power at court. Yushi, considering himself a close kinsman of the state, remonstrated often and thereby incurred jealousy. The generals all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yi was enthroned, his uncle Yang Liangjie held court power. Yushi, as imperial kin, remonstrated often, earned jealousy, and was feared by the generals.

sentences.zh: 未幾，北兵逼浙東，乃命與檡出瑞安，與守臣方洪共任備禦。

translations.literal: Before long the Northern Army pressed Eastern Zhe. He was then ordered to go out to Ruian, where together with the defending official Fang Hong he bore responsibility for defense preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Soon northern forces pressed Eastern Zhe. He was sent to Ruian to share defense duties with defender Fang Hong.

sentences.zh: 朝臣言與檡有劉更生之忠，曹王皋之孝，宜留輔以隆國本。

translations.literal: Court ministers said Yushi had the loyalty of Liu Gengsheng and the filial piety of Cao Wanggao, and ought to be kept to assist the throne and strengthen the foundation of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers said Yushi had Liu Gengsheng's loyalty and Cao Wanggao's filial devotion and should remain at court to strengthen the throne.

sentences.zh: 譖者益急，卒遣之。

translations.literal: Slanderers grew more urgent, and in the end he was sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Slander grew fiercer, and in the end he was sent away.

sentences.zh: 瑞安受圍，城中危急，與洪誓以死守。

translations.literal: Ruian was besieged and the city was in peril. He and Hong swore to defend to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Ruian was besieged and the city desperate. He and Hong swore to hold to the death.

sentences.zh: 小校李雄夜開門納外兵，與檡、洪率眾巷戰，兵敗被縶，董文炳問之曰：“汝為秀王耶？

translations.literal: A petty officer, Li Xiong, opened the gate by night and admitted the outside army. Yushi and Hong led the masses in street fighting. The army was defeated and they were bound. Dong Wenbing questioned him, saying, "Are you the Prince of Xiù?
translations.idiomatic: Petty officer Li Xiong opened the gates by night and let the enemy in. Yushi and Hong led street fighting, were beaten and seized. Dong Wenbing asked, "Are you the Prince of Xiù?

sentences.zh: 今能降乎？”

translations.literal: Can you surrender now?"
translations.idiomatic: Will you surrender now?

sentences.zh: 與檡厲聲曰：“我國家近親，今力屈而死，分也，尚何問為？”

translations.literal: Yushi said in a harsh voice, "I am a close kinsman of the state. Now my strength is spent and I die — that is my portion. What is there still to ask?"
translations.idiomatic: Yushi cried harshly, "I am the emperor's close kin. My strength is spent and I die — that is fate. What more is there to ask?"

sentences.zh: 遂殺之。

translations.literal: They then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They killed him.

sentences.zh: 洪亦伏節而死。

translations.literal: Hong also upheld his integrity and died.
translations.idiomatic: Hong too upheld his integrity and died.

sentences.zh: 又有趙孟錦者，少不羈，遊淮以軍功為將佐。

translations.literal: There was also Zhao Mengjin, unrestrained in youth, who traveled the Huai region and through military merit became a general's aide.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Zhao Mengjin — wild in youth, who won a general's post on the Huai through military merit.

sentences.zh: 北兵攻真州，每戰輒為士卒先，守苗再成倚之為重。

translations.literal: When the Northern Army attacked Zhenzhou, in every battle he was first among the soldiers. The defender Miao Zaicheng relied on him as a mainstay.
translations.idiomatic: When the north attacked Zhenzhou, he led every charge. Defender Miao Zaicheng leaned on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 北兵重艦駐江上，孟錦乘大霧來襲，俄霧解，日已高，北兵見其兵少，逐之，登舟失足墮水，身荷重甲，溺焉。

translations.literal: The Northern Army's heavy ships lay at anchor on the river. Mengjin took advantage of heavy fog to come and strike. Soon the fog lifted and the sun was already high. The Northern Army saw his force was few and pursued him. Boarding a boat he lost his footing and fell into the water. His body bore heavy armor, and he drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Northern heavy ships lay in the river. Mengjin struck through thick fog; when it lifted and the sun rose high, the enemy saw how few he was and pursued. Boarding a boat he slipped into the water in full armor and drowned.

sentences.zh: 趙淮，丞相葵之從子也。

translations.literal: Zhao Huai was the Chancellor Kui's younger cousin's son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Huai was a nephew of Chancellor Li Kui.

sentences.zh: 李全之叛，屢立戰功，累官至淮東轉運使。

translations.literal: When Li Quan rebelled, he repeatedly won battle merit and rose through offices to Huai-East Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Quan rebelled, he won repeated battle honors and rose to Huai-East transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 德祐中，戍銀樹埧，兵敗，與其妾俱被執至瓜州，元帥阿術使淮招李庭芝，許以大官。

translations.literal: In Deyou he garrisoned Yingshu Ford, was defeated in battle, and together with his concubine was seized and taken to Guazhou. The Yuan marshal Aju had Huai summon Li Tingzhi, promising him a great office.
translations.idiomatic: During Deyou he garrisoned Yingshu Ford, was defeated, and was taken with his concubine to Guazhou. Yuan marshal Aju had Huai summon Li Tingzhi with promises of high office.

sentences.zh: 淮陽許諾，至揚城下，乃大呼曰：“李庭芝！

translations.literal: Huai falsely assented. When he reached below Yang city he then shouted, "Li Tingzhi!
translations.idiomatic: Huai feigned agreement. At the walls of Yangzhou he shouted, "Li Tingzhi!

sentences.zh: 男子死耳，毋降也！”

translations.literal: A man dies — that is all. Do not surrender!"
translations.idiomatic: Men die — that is all there is to it. Do not yield!

sentences.zh: 元帥怒，殺之，棄屍江濱。

translations.literal: The marshal was angry, killed him, and cast his corpse on the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: The marshal was enraged, killed him, and cast his body on the riverbank.
